description: CI tier definition (ADR-2169). The one place that says which pull requests run which part of the suite. scripts/ci/ci_tier.py decides the tier of an event, .github/workflows/ci-tier.yml hands the decision to every workflow, and the Required Checks Aggregator reads this file to know which required contexts a tier does not owe.

tiers.full: Every event that is not a pull request from this repository (master push, dispatch, schedule), every fork pull request, an own pull request labelled `ci: full`, and a release pull request labelled `autorelease: cut`. Runs the whole suite.
tiers.light: A pull request whose head repository is this repository (Renovate included). Runs lint, format, the fast suite and the governance gates; the contexts in `full_only` are not run.
tiers.release-light: The machine-generated release pull request without the cut label. Runs the contexts in `always` only.

own_input_lanes.reason: A full-only context whose lane also runs on a light-tier pull request, but only when the diff touches an input the lane reads (selectors of .github/ci-impact.json, ADR-2198): the Windows zip legs failed on master for two days because a pull request that changed their inputs never built them (ADR-1595 built the x64 zip only, ADR-2169 built nothing).

untiered_jobs.reason: The aggregator is the merge gate: it reads the tier itself and must fail, not skip, on a draft (a skipped required context would count as passing).
Owed by every tier: it proves that the release cut ran and is the one check a release pull request keeps without the cut label.
pull_request_target label job: one API call, writes a label, runs no repository code. It does not run on synchronize.
Starts the full suite when `ci: full` or `autorelease: cut` is applied; skipped for every other label.
Opt-in lane: the gate job starts only for a ready pull request that carries the label `run-e2e-k8s` (ADR-0783); every other job of the workflow follows it.

Opt-in lane, not required (Q-194): the gate job starts only for a ready pull request that carries the label `run-observability-smoke`; the smoke job follows it. Nightly and dispatch runs are the full tier.

Praetor-managed, byte-locked by `praetorctl audit`. Since praetor#815 its first step fails closed on a draft and every later step is skipped, so a draft does no work, but the job itself still starts and reports a red check, which the tier's job-level gate cannot express. `test_praetor_managed_jobs_stop_on_a_draft_before_any_work` proves the step shape.

Written by praetor (ADR-2784) and kept in its hosted gate shape, edited only to pin the actions to commits: its first step fails closed on a draft and every later step is skipped, so a draft does no work, but the job itself still starts and reports a red check. A job-level skip would report success on a draft, which praetor's audit warns against. `test_praetor_managed_jobs_stop_on_a_draft_before_any_work` proves the step shape.
